text:
sara: FYI onboarding Memento-7B (converted from Mistral checkpoints) — ran quick int4 pass and saw a consistent ROUGE/BLEU delta and a small long-context drift when inputs include combining diacritics and emoji ZWJ sequences.
sara: baseline fp16 Rouge-L 40.2 -> int4 36.1. BLEU 22.0 -> 19.3. perplexity dev 11.8 -> 14.9.
kevin: did you run a token-map diff? conversion tooling sometimes collapses emoji zwj sequences into single tokens or shifts around combining diacritics.
sara: yes `scripts/token_map_check.py` showed ~0.22% mismatched ids. Mostly contiguous runs around 0x0300-0x036F and some around 0x1F3FB-0x1F3FF (skin tone modifiers). sample:
```text
orig token id 0x0308 -> 17902
conv token id 0x0308 -> 17903
orig token id 0x1F469 0x200D 0x1F4BB -> [345, 200, 789] (three tokens)
conv token id 0x1F469 0x200D 0x1F4BB -> [345, 201, 789] (middle token +1)
```
sara: interestingly the worst-performing evals are where the reference includes accented characters and ZWJ-joined emoji sequences.
tom: also check rotary/freq params — when we reshape heads during conversion some codepaths changed head-ordering. a headwise-permute can cause the rotary to be applied to wrong head vectors resulting in slow factual drift.
kevin: quick check I run locally:
```bash
python - <<'PY'
import torch
c = torch.load('memento_conv.pt', map_location='cpu')
print('rotary.shape', c['rotary.freq'].shape)
print('rotary[:8]', c['rotary.freq'][:8])
print('head_order_hint', c.get('meta.head_order',''))
PY
```
kevin: the converted checkpoint has rotary.freq values but no head_order metadata, and freq array looks permuted vs our Mistral reference.
sara: eval-bot: redwood-evals run 2026-03-24T09:03Z (summarization-small + emoji-accent subset)
```text
suite: summarization-small, emoji-accent-subset
models: fp16_memento, int4_memento_conv
fp16_memento: Rouge-L 40.2, BLEU 22.0
int4_memento_conv: Rouge-L 36.1, BLEU 19.3
observations: failures concentrated on sentences with multiple combining marks or ZWJ-joined emoji; qualitative checks show token-level id shifts and occasional token dropout at emoji boundaries.
```
sara: hypothesis: two stacked issues: (1) tokenizer normalizer discrepancy (NFC vs NFKC) causing contiguous id offsets in combining ranges, (2) head-index permutation after weight reshape so rotary application mismatches head vectors. either alone causes small regressions; together they amplify.
tom: mitigation plan: A) create a thin remap layer at load time that maps conv token ids -> original ids and remap embedding indices (cheap, fast). B) permute rotary arrays and q/k/v heads to match original ordering before int4 serialization (medium). C) long-term: make conversion emit `meta.head_order` and preserve tokenizer normalizer flags.
kevin: I'll try A and B separately on dev snapshot tonight and run the emoji-accent eval slice. can someone queue a dev snapshot?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: queued snapshot `memento-conv-int4-remap-20260324` (req: rq_b12f). ETA ~40m.
sara: thanks. quick note: when remapping embeddings, be careful to also remap any tied weights (output/ln_f embeddings) and check tied-shared flags. we tripped this once with Lyra onboarding.
tom: also monitor kvcache warmup traces — if rotary/hotkey mismatch, attention attention-scores heatmap will show banding across head index after ~256 tokens. put a heatmap hook in the dev run.
kevin: logging plan: dump token-delta histogram, run Rouge-L on emoji-accent subset, kvcache-heatmap after 1k tokens. will post results in this thread.
sara: brilliant. tagging @kevin @tom. grab coffee, will check in later. :sparkles:
